title: わざわざ — “go to the trouble of ～ / specially”
summary: An adverb that says someone took extra trouble, time or effort to do something that was not strictly necessary. Often used to thank someone (わざわざありがとう) or to say something is worth the effort.

patterns.form: わざわざ＋動詞（てくれる／に来る／に行く など）
patterns.gloss: specially do ～ / go out of the way to ～

patterns.form: わざわざ＋動詞＋のに／ても
patterns.gloss: even though one took the trouble (often regretful)

body.p: わざわざ stresses that the person went beyond what was needed. わざわざ来てくれてありがとう: thank you for coming all this way. It is frequently combined with ～てくれる to show gratitude.
It can also say something is worth the trouble: わざわざ買いに行く価値がある. And it can express regret when the effort was wasted: わざわざ行ったのに閉まっていた.

body.h: Do not confuse with わざと
body.p: わざと means “deliberately, for a hidden reason”. わざわざ means “taking special trouble”. わざわざ is about effort and consideration, not about intent to tease or hurt.

examples.ja: わざわざ来（き）てくれてありがとう。
examples.tr: Thank you for going out of your way to come.

examples.ja: 忙（いそが）しいのに、わざわざ手伝（てつだ）いに来（き）てくれた。
examples.romaji: Isogashii noni, wazawaza tetsudai ni kite kureta.
examples.tr: Even though they were busy, they went out of their way to come and help.

examples.ja: この店（みせ）のケーキは、わざわざ買（か）いに行（い）く価値（かち）がある。
examples.romaji: Kono mise no keeki wa, wazawaza kai ni iku kachi ga aru.
examples.tr: This shop’s cake is worth going out of your way to buy.

pitfalls: Do not use it for something you do every day as a routine; it needs extra effort beyond the usual.
わざわざ and わざと are different words. Check which one you mean.
